title: Asaka Performs 'Tetsuryō! meet with Tetsudō Musume' Anime's Opening Song
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter ) account for Tetsuryō! meet with Tetsudō Musume , the original television anime based on the Tetsudō Musume (Railway Girls) characters, announced on Sunday that artist Asaka is performing the anime's opening theme song "GO! GO! RAILWAY!!"

The original anime's story centers on four train-loving college students who are members of the Tetsudō Ryokō Dōkō-kai ("Tetsuryo" in short, or literally Railway Travel Club). They journey throughout the world where hundreds of Tetsudō Musume work.

The anime will star:

• May Tachibana as Misaki Sata

• Mao Shōji as Kodama Orihara

• Haruna Fukushima as Ushio Yagami

• Hika Tsukishiro as Usa Harutachi

• Fūka Izumi as Yayoi Nakano

• Yukari Anzai as Arisa Nishiura

• Yuki Nakashima as Chihaya Asakura

• Asami Seto as Sakie Ashio

• Hana Hishikawa as Shiina Igusa

• Ayaka Ōhashi as Juri Okuwa

• Hikaru Tohno as Sia Kasukabe

• Yūki Tenma as Misya Kamii

• Yurika Kubo as Ibuki Kawagoe

• Misaki Kuno as Miyabi Kinugawa

• Mana Kumasaki as Akana Kurihashi

• Minami Takahashi as Misaki Kо̄jiro

• Haruki Iwata as Minano Sakurazawa

• Nene Hieda as Konomi Shibaguchi

• Iori Saeki as Azami Takashima

• Misa Segawa as Izumi Tachikawa

• Suzuka Hara as Tsukushi Togawa

• Kana Ichinose as Karen Matsukaze

• Shiori Mikami as Kinu Watarase

TOMYTEC is credited for the original work in collaboration with I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level novel writer Kisetsu Morita . Misuzu Hoshino ( Laid-Back Camp episode director, Hokkaido Gals Are Super Adorable! , The Maid I Hired Recently Is Mysterious director) is directing the anime at East Fish Studio . Aya Satsuki ( Solo Camping for Two , "Ippon" Again! , Too Cute Crisis ) is overseeing and writing the series scripts, and Hisanori Hashimoto ( Laid-Back Camp season 3) is designing the characters. The Tetsuryo Club, comprised of the main voice actors: May Tachibana (Misaki), Mao Shōji (Kodama), Haruna Fukushima (Ushio), and Hika Tsukishiro (Usa) will perform the ending theme song "Watashi Miraisen" (My Future Line).

The anime will premiere on October 8 at 12:00 a.m. JST (effectively, October 9 at midnight) on the Tokyo MX and BS Fuji channels. HIDIVE will stream the anime as it airs in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand. This year's Anime NYC event hosted the anime's world premiere on August 21.

The Tetsudō Musume characters "work" in railway companies and railway-related businesses all over Japan, wearing real uniforms and work clothes. As of May 2025, there are 114 Tetsudō Musume all over Japan. Tetsudō Musume launched in 2005, and celebrated its 20th anniversary in 2025.
author: ANN

title: Shogakukan Launches 'Rumiko Takahashi Fantasy Manga Awards'
content:
This year's 42nd and 43rd combined issue of Shogakukan 's Weekly Shonen Sunday magazine announced its new " Rumiko Takahashi Fantasy Manga Awards" on Wednesday, and the organizers are currently accepting manga entries until January 11, 2027.

The contest is open to professional and amateur manga creators. Entries must be 42 pages or less and contain at least one fantasy element. Takahashi will head the panel of judges which will also include Weekly Shonen Sunday editor-in-chief Kazunori Ōshima and other Shonen Sunday editors. The organizers will announce the results in Weekly Shonen Sunday and on the awards' website on March 24.

The grand prize winner will receive 1 million yen (about US$6,000), and their manga will be published in Weekly Shonen Sunday or a spinoff publication and on Shogakukan 's Sunday Webry manga website. The second prize winner will get 500,000 yen (about US$3,000), and their manga will also be published in Weekly Shonen Sunday or a spinoff publication and on Sunday Webry . The honorable mention recipient will receivie 300,000 yen (about US$2,000), and their work will appear on Sunday Webry . The effort prize recipient will receive 100,000 yen (about US$600), and the encouragement prize recipient will receive 30,000 yen (about US$200).

Takahashi debuted as a manga creator in 1978, and in her career of over three decades, Takahashi has created manga such as Urusei Yatsura , Maison Ikkoku , Mermaid Saga , Rumic Theater , Ranma 1/2 , One-Pound Gospel , and Inuyasha . Many of her works have become internationally popular and inspired anime and live-action adaptations.

The compiled volumes of all of Takahashi's manga have surpassed 230 million copies in circulation worldwide, as of August 2024.

The anime adaptation of Takahashi's MAO manga premiered on April 4, and is running for two continuous cours (quarter of a year).

The third season of the new anime based on Takahashi's Ranma 1/2 manga will debut on October 3.

A new television anime of Takahashi's Urusei Yatsura manga premiered in October 2022. The anime's first half ran for half a year, or two cours without breaks. The show's second half aired for two consecutive cours and started in January 2024. The show's fourth and final cours premiered in April that same year.

title: Mazenchu Food Characters Get TV Anime on October 7
content:
Graphic design company Torch announced on Wednesday that its Mazenchu character brand will receive a anime that will begin airing as the first original anime within Kansai TV 's morning news and lifestyle program Yoidon! on October 7.

Mazenchu is set in a school where all kinds of food can live out their youth and form friendships, rivalries, and bittersweet romances.

The cast includes:

• Obara Rea as Sume, a sushi rice girl

• Sakura Hayashi as Abo, an avocado girl

• Uki Nashiki as Akami, a tuna boy

• Kokoro Kikuchi as Shinko, a pickled vegetable boy

Ebi created the Mazenchu characters. Yuusuke Takase (CG on Berserk: The Golden Age Arc I - The Egg of the King , Halo Legends , Detroit Metal City ) is directing the anime at Studio Nanahoshi . The studio dugout is producing the sound, and Aiin is producing the music. Bonjin is the offline editor. Liberty Animation Studio produced the opening animation. Sayo Kawase is the executive producer, and Torch is planning and producing the project.

title: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Reveals 11 Character Posters Ahead of October Premiere
content:
The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 has revealed a new set of 11 character posters ahead of its October 2, 2026 premiere. It will lead up to the upcoming movie , which will premiere in Japan on December 11 with an original story by the author Natsu Hyuuga. The second cour of Season 3 is scheduled for April 2027.

The anime previously revealed a teaser trailer featuring the opening theme song “Kumo wo Nuke Kazashimo e Watashi Dake” by Yorushika. Studio OLM is back to handle the animation production, while TOHO animation STUDIO is notably absent from the staff credits list.

You can see the new character posters below.

ALSO READ: The Apothecary Diaries Interview: Aoi Yuki (Maomao) & Takeo Otsuka (Jinshi) Crunchyroll Reveals New York Comic Con 2026 Lineup With The Apothecary Diaries, Sentenced to Be a Hero, Black Clover and More

You can watch the trailer for the anime below.

The main staff was also previously revealed and includes:

• Director: Akinori Fudesaka

• Assistant Director: Wataru Nakagawa

• Series Composition: Norihiro Naganuma

• Scripts: Yuko Kakihara, Misuzu Chiba, Hitomi Ogawa

• Character Design: Yukiko Nakatani

• Art Director: Katsumi Takao

• Color Design: Misato Aida, Nanako Okazaki

• CGI Director: Tamotsu Nagai

• Director of Photography: Mayo Suzuki

• Editing: Daisuke Imai

• Sound Director: Shoji Hata

• Music: Satoru Kosaki, Kevin Penkin, Arisa Okehazama

• Animation Production: OLM

You can also see the key visual:

Natsu Hyuga writes the The Apothecary Diaries light novel, with illustrations by Toko Shino. The series is serialized by Shunfunotomo. The series has 2 manga adaptations, one written by Itsuki Nanao and illustrated by Nekokurage, and one written and illustrated by Minoji Kurata.

J-Novel Club is publishing the novel in English, while Squre Enix is publishing the manga. The story follows Maomao, a young apothecary who ends up getting sold to the emperor’s palace as a lowly servant. She’s not the type of character who can just stay obedient, so she ends up helping Jinshi, the handsome official at the palace.

The franchise recently also announced its first live-action series adaptation , as well as the first console game .

title: The Road to Redemption: Unmasking The Vermilion Mask
content:
Combining dark fantasy, action, and an unconventional approach to the shounen genre, Shuiro no Kamen ( The Vermilion Mask ) is set to bring its striking world and mysterious masks to television this October. From its first chapters, the manga stands out for its willingness to place its protagonist in situations rarely seen in shounen stories, forcing him to confront guilt, loss, and the consequences of his actions rather than simply growing stronger.

At Anime Expo 2026, we had the opportunity to speak with the manga editor Taichi Kimura and Taihi Kimura , the voice of Peru, the central character of the series. Together, they offered insight into what makes Peru such an unusual and compelling protagonist, the creative decisions behind some of the manga's most unexpected developments, and the relationships that gradually take shape as he moves forward.

──As an editor, what stood out to you the most when you first came across the manga, and what made you believe it had the potential to resonate with readers?

Editor Taichi Kimura: When I first looked at the storyboard for chapter one, I asked the author, "What happens next?" and had him guide me through the overall plot up to around the third chapter. After hearing that, I was amazed at how fast-paced the story was. It contained developments that you don't normally see in shounen manga, so many story points came as a surprise.

The themes are a bit dark, but I felt that having a shounen manga character confront his need for redemption and face his struggles with a more positive outlook would give readers something they could relate to, making the character very easy to empathize with.

──As the voice of the lead character Peru, could you tell us how you became involved with The Vermilion Mask ?

Seiyuu Taihi Kimura: When I was given the opportunity to audition for The Vermilion Mask , I read the original manga. I thought it was very interesting, so it took me only a day to read through everything, and I went into the audition really hoping that I would get the role. Then, as fate would have it, I was given the opportunity to play Peru.

At the time of the audition, I wouldn't say I felt overly confident about it, but it went pretty smoothly. There weren't many corrections or retakes, and it went by quite quickly. I typically land the part when I have really good feelings about the audition, so I was very happy when I heard I got the role.

Editor Kimura: Director Watanabe said, "I already envision Kimura-san as the role." But these weren't only the director's thoughts. The voice we heard in the audition matched Peru's character perfectly, and the line readings were exceptional, so it was a unanimous decision.

Seiyuu Kimura: Ah, thank you very much. It makes me happy to hear that.

──This is your second leading role in an anime series. How does it feel?

Seiyuu Kimura: I'm very happy. Incredibly happy, with a bit of nervousness too, but I want to enjoy myself as much as I can while doing it.

──What are some appealing points of Peru's character? Please tell us what you kept in mind when recording.

Seiyuu Kimura: I think part of Peru's charm comes from the fact that he's still a child. He tends to take too much on himself, which is worrisome, but this is also what makes you grow fond of him. I like how strong his sense of responsibility is, his feelings of, "I have to be the one to do it."

Although he is a pretty quiet character, or rather, a cool and reserved character, I keep in mind that even Peru laughs. Like a normal human being, he has a wide range of emotions, and even though he's cool, he has a boyish side that's appropriate for his age. That's the part of him I try to not forget.

"Seeing how he comes to terms with his guilt and how he can gradually move forward makes him a character that you want to cheer on."

──Something shocking and irreversible happens to Peru early in the story, which we rarely see happen to a main character. Without spoiling anything, could you tell us how you felt about that development?

Editor Kimura: Part of me wondered how readers would react to the fact that he commits a crime, but at the same time, he goes through an incredibly painful experience. Seeing how he comes to terms with his guilt and how he can gradually move forward makes him a character that you want to cheer on.

Seiyuu Kimura: I think Peru is definitely a character who tends to put the blame on himself, but I think how he grows from that point onward is what's important. Even though he finds himself in a difficult situation, it can't simply end with his death. I feel like what comes after is what is so important about Peru as a character, and really, the entire story itself. I hope that seeing Pelle smile will allow others to smile with him as well.

Editor Kimura: Also, something unfortunate happens to him around the second episode. I can't go into too much detail because it would be a spoiler, but I think once you see it, he will become a character you really want to root for.

──Actually, I think that event in the second episode might be what I was referring to.

About his arm? Both: Oh! About his arm! Editor Kimura: As I mentioned earlier, I had heard this event would happen when we were working on the first chapter, and I remember thinking it would have a huge impact. It is also something that doesn't usually happen to the main character, so I personally found it incredibly fresh and unique, really unlike anything I'd seen before. So, it sounded like a good idea at the time, but it became quite inconvenient actually. Manga is often made one chapter at a time, so you make the general outline and work towards it with certain milestones. Since we didn't really think that far ahead, after the event happened, we were really in big trouble, thinking things like, "Oh no, what do we do?" and "Without his arm, he can't make masks then." Seiyuu Kimura: It’s hard to imagine, isn’t it? From my perspective, it would be like losing the ability to talk. Peru is such a tragic character. Even though he was rescued from being abandoned and nearly dead once, after that he almost dies again. And then after that, he loses his life's work, which is almost like he died yet again. A lot of protagonists these days gain things as the story goes on, but Peru just keeps losing things, so I wonder if he'll be okay. I feel sorry for him.

──Are there any other scenes or characters that left a strong impression on you?

Seiyuu Kimura: Totoque, a character that appears in the first episode. He's in the PV, too. I recommend looking out for him. He's a bit psychopathic, something just feels off about him. But he's very handsome! (in English)

Editor Kimura: There's a character named Moku who joins the group and uses smoke as his fighting ability. The relationship between him and Peru stands out. As the story progresses, Moku becomes a character who helps shoulder some of the responsibility Peru is carrying, and the scenes where he fights for Peru's sake increase. I highly recommend paying attention to their relationship and the "buddy" dynamic that develops between them.

──By "buddy" dynamic, do you mean they become very close friends?

Editor Kimura: I wouldn't go that far. They become a bit closer than before, but it's more like allies who are standing together in battle. Similar to Zenitsu and Tanjirou from Kimetsu no Yaiba . (everyone laughs)

"Both of them are trying to make amends for what they've done, and since their circumstances are alike, both of them want to be forgiven by the other."

──Since we haven't talked about Sonah yet, what do you find most interesting about the relationship dynamics between the three main characters (Peru, Sonah, and Moku)?

Seiyuu Kimura: It's tough to think of something the three of them have in common. Each of them have a different role, as they move along they slowly become more open and grow together.

Editor Kimura: Peru and Sonah find themselves in a similar situation, as both have committed a sin. Both of them are trying to make amends for what they've done, and since their circumstances are alike, both of them want to be forgiven by the other. That becomes a crucial part of their relationship. And I think how Moku takes care of others, like a mischievous oniichan from the neighborhood, is really great.

──Do you have any memorable moments you can share from the recording sessions with the other cast and staff?

Seiyuu Kimura: There were actually quite a few amusing moments, which one would be best? …Hang on, this is actually kinda hard. Let me think for a minute.

Editor Kimura: The three main cast members are Kimura-san, Yamamoto-san (who plays Sonah), and Ura-san (who plays Moku). When the three of them are standing next to each other during the recording and you see them from behind, their heights are similar to their characters. Their dynamic can also kind of feel like they're really Peru, Sonah, and Moku, so sometimes I just find myself watching their interactions play out.

Seiyuu Kimura: Back in high school, I used to perform dramatic readings as part of my club activities. It turns out that Yamamoto-san, who plays Sonah, is the same age as me and was in the same type of club. Apparently, Yamamoto-san already knew who I was.

Editor Kimura: Oh, really? Was it because you were the best?

Seiyuu Kimura: No no, it's not like that. She apparently knew about me from a contest. When she said to me, "I already know about you~", I realized she must have been close by. That's scary, I thought.

Editor Kimura: You even participated in the same competition.

Seiyuu Kimura: And then our paths crossed again here.

Editor Kimura: That's a wonderful story.

"Well, with the mind control mask, I could really do anything. Like using it to make the people who cause trouble do volunteer work."

──There are many different masks with different levels and powers. Which mask interests you the most so far and what would you do with it?

Editor Kimura: I'd go for the dragon mask. Then if I ever had an awful day at work or something, I could use it to vent my frustrations somewhere deep in the mountains.

Seiyuu Kimura: (laughs) Wouldn't you want to use it to trash the company instead?

Editor Kimura: I would definitely feel too guilty for that. What about you?

Seiyuu Kimura: Well, with the mind control mask, I could really do anything. Like using it to make the people who cause trouble do volunteer work. (laughs)

Editor Kimura: Amazing.

Seiyuu Kimura: It sounds really bad saying it like that, but it's not a bad thing.

Editor Kimura: No, it's really great.

──Please leave a final message for the MyAnimeList community.

Seiyuu Kimura: This series has turned out to be incredibly entertaining, so I really want you to watch the first episode. Once you see it, I think you'll get a good feel for what the world and series is like, so please be sure to check it out.

Editor Kimura: I feel like the level of awareness and enthusiasm for the upcoming anime does not match the incredible amount of passion that went into creating it, so I'm really counting on anime fans in MyAnimeList's community to help spread the word. I'm confident this is going to be an amazing series. If you watch the first episode, I think you’ll fall in love with it, so I hope you'll check it out.

Interview was conducted through an interpreter and has been edited for clarity.

Editor Kimura: Director Watanabe said, "I already envision Kimura-san as the role." But these weren't only the director's thoughts. The voice we heard in the audition matched Peru's character perfectly, and the line readings were exceptional, so it was a unanimous decision.
Seiyuu Kimura: Ah, thank you very much. It makes me happy to hear that.
──This is your second leading role in an anime series. How does it feel?
Seiyuu Kimura: I'm very happy. Incredibly happy, with a bit of nervousness too, but I want to enjoy myself as much as I can while doing it.
──What are some appealing points of Peru's character? Please tell us what you kept in mind when recording.

Seiyuu Kimura: I think part of Peru's charm comes from the fact that he's still a child. He tends to take too much on himself, which is worrisome, but this is also what makes you grow fond of him. I like how strong his sense of responsibility is, his feelings of, "I have to be the one to do it."

Although he is a pretty quiet character, or rather, a cool and reserved character, I keep in mind that even Peru laughs. Like a normal human being, he has a wide range of emotions, and even though he's cool, he has a boyish side that's appropriate for his age. That's the part of him I try to not forget.
"Seeing how he comes to terms with his guilt and how he can gradually move forward makes him a character that you want to cheer on."

──Something shocking and irreversible happens to Peru early in the story, which we rarely see happen to a main character. Without spoiling anything, could you tell us how you felt about that development?

Editor Kimura: Part of me wondered how readers would react to the fact that he commits a crime, but at the same time, he goes through an incredibly painful experience. Seeing how he comes to terms with his guilt and how he can gradually move forward makes him a character that you want to cheer on.

Seiyuu Kimura: I think Peru is definitely a character who tends to put the blame on himself, but I think how he grows from that point onward is what's important. Even though he finds himself in a difficult situation, it can't simply end with his death. I feel like what comes after is what is so important about Peru as a character, and really, the entire story itself. I hope that seeing Pelle smile will allow others to smile with him as well.

Editor Kimura: Also, something unfortunate happens to him around the second episode. I can't go into too much detail because it would be a spoiler, but I think once you see it, he will become a character you really want to root for.
──Actually, I think that event in the second episode might be what I was referring to.

About his arm? Both: Oh! About his arm! Editor Kimura: As I mentioned earlier, I had heard this event would happen when we were working on the first chapter, and I remember thinking it would have a huge impact. It is also something that doesn't usually happen to the main character, so I personally found it incredibly fresh and unique, really unlike anything I'd seen before. So, it sounded like a good idea at the time, but it became quite inconvenient actually. Manga is often made one chapter at a time, so you make the general outline and work towards it with certain milestones. Since we didn't really think that far ahead, after the event happened, we were really in big trouble, thinking things like, "Oh no, what do we do?" and "Without his arm, he can't make masks then." Seiyuu Kimura: It’s hard to imagine, isn’t it? From my perspective, it would be like losing the ability to talk. Peru is such a tragic character. Even though he was rescued from being abandoned and nearly dead once, after that he almost dies again. And then after that, he loses his life's work, which is almost like he died yet again. A lot of protagonists these days gain things as the story goes on, but Peru just keeps losing things, so I wonder if he'll be okay. I feel sorry for him.
──Are there any other scenes or characters that left a strong impression on you?

Seiyuu Kimura: Totoque, a character that appears in the first episode. He's in the PV, too. I recommend looking out for him. He's a bit psychopathic, something just feels off about him. But he's very handsome! (in English)

Editor Kimura: There's a character named Moku who joins the group and uses smoke as his fighting ability. The relationship between him and Peru stands out. As the story progresses, Moku becomes a character who helps shoulder some of the responsibility Peru is carrying, and the scenes where he fights for Peru's sake increase. I highly recommend paying attention to their relationship and the "buddy" dynamic that develops between them.
──By "buddy" dynamic, do you mean they become very close friends?

Editor Kimura: I wouldn't go that far. They become a bit closer than before, but it's more like allies who are standing together in battle. Similar to Zenitsu and Tanjirou from Kimetsu no Yaiba . (everyone laughs)
"Both of them are trying to make amends for what they've done, and since their circumstances are alike, both of them want to be forgiven by the other."
──Since we haven't talked about Sonah yet, what do you find most interesting about the relationship dynamics between the three main characters (Peru, Sonah, and Moku)?
Seiyuu Kimura: It's tough to think of something the three of them have in common. Each of them have a different role, as they move along they slowly become more open and grow together.

Editor Kimura: Peru and Sonah find themselves in a similar situation, as both have committed a sin. Both of them are trying to make amends for what they've done, and since their circumstances are alike, both of them want to be forgiven by the other. That becomes a crucial part of their relationship. And I think how Moku takes care of others, like a mischievous oniichan from the neighborhood, is really great.
──Do you have any memorable moments you can share from the recording sessions with the other cast and staff?
Seiyuu Kimura: There were actually quite a few amusing moments, which one would be best? …Hang on, this is actually kinda hard. Let me think for a minute.

Editor Kimura: The three main cast members are Kimura-san, Yamamoto-san (who plays Sonah), and Ura-san (who plays Moku). When the three of them are standing next to each other during the recording and you see them from behind, their heights are similar to their characters. Their dynamic can also kind of feel like they're really Peru, Sonah, and Moku, so sometimes I just find myself watching their interactions play out.

Seiyuu Kimura: Back in high school, I used to perform dramatic readings as part of my club activities. It turns out that Yamamoto-san, who plays Sonah, is the same age as me and was in the same type of club. Apparently, Yamamoto-san already knew who I was.
Editor Kimura: Oh, really? Was it because you were the best?

Seiyuu Kimura: No no, it's not like that. She apparently knew about me from a contest. When she said to me, "I already know about you~", I realized she must have been close by. That's scary, I thought.
Editor Kimura: You even participated in the same competition.
Seiyuu Kimura: And then our paths crossed again here.
Editor Kimura: That's a wonderful story.
"Well, with the mind control mask, I could really do anything. Like using it to make the people who cause trouble do volunteer work."
──There are many different masks with different levels and powers. Which mask interests you the most so far and what would you do with it?
Editor Kimura: I'd go for the dragon mask. Then if I ever had an awful day at work or something, I could use it to vent my frustrations somewhere deep in the mountains.
Seiyuu Kimura: (laughs) Wouldn't you want to use it to trash the company instead?
Editor Kimura: I would definitely feel too guilty for that. What about you?
Seiyuu Kimura: Well, with the mind control mask, I could really do anything. Like using it to make the people who cause trouble do volunteer work. (laughs)
Editor Kimura: Amazing.
Seiyuu Kimura: It sounds really bad saying it like that, but it's not a bad thing.
Editor Kimura: No, it's really great.
──Please leave a final message for the MyAnimeList community.

Seiyuu Kimura: This series has turned out to be incredibly entertaining, so I really want you to watch the first episode. Once you see it, I think you'll get a good feel for what the world and series is like, so please be sure to check it out.

Editor Kimura: I feel like the level of awareness and enthusiasm for the upcoming anime does not match the incredible amount of passion that went into creating it, so I'm really counting on anime fans in MyAnimeList's community to help spread the word. I'm confident this is going to be an amazing series. If you watch the first episode, I think you’ll fall in love with it, so I hope you'll check it out.
Interview was conducted through an interpreter and has been edited for clarity.

title: Witch and Mercenary Anime's New Video Unveils More Cast & Staff, April 2027 Debut
content:
Bandai Namco Filmworks unveiled the first full promotional video and new visuals for the television anime of Kaeru Chōhōkiteki 's Witch and Mercenary ( Majo to Yōhei ) light novel series on Wednesday. The video announces more cast and staff members, as well as the anime's April 2027 premiere date.

The anime will premiere on NTV and 29 other affiliated channels as well as on the satellite channel BS NTV in April 2027.

The newly announced cast members are:

Yuri Noguchi as Isana Gihon, a swordmaster (adventurer rank 2) nicknamed "Snow White"

Hiromu Mineta as Alan Clows, a swordmaster (adventurer rank 4) and party leader

Haruka Shiraishi as Elicia Armel, a mysterious staff-wielding adventurer (rank 3)

The new staff members include:

• Assistant Series Script Supervisor: Shingo Irie

• Sub-Character Design: Hideki Sakai

• Monster Design: Wataru Inada, Ryō Hirada

• Chief Animation Directors: Keita Matsumoto, Hideki Sakai, Sorato Shimizu

• Art: Sorato Shimizu

• Art Director: Kazuhiro Inoue

• Prop Design: Mikio

• Image Boards: pomodorosa

• Color Key Artist: Kunio Tsujita

• Compositing Director of Photography: Shūhei Inabe

• CG Director: Fūma Aizawa

• Editing: Gō Sadamatsu

The previously announced cast members include:

Saori Hayami as Siasha

Taito Ban as Zig Crane

Seven Seas Entertainment releases the novels in English and describes the story:

Nothing in this world is more dangerous than a witch. The epitome of fear and terror, they can summon floods on a whim, conjure balls of fire out of the air, or even destroy entire countries overnight. Incur their wrath, and no one is safe. At least, that's what everyone thinks, and it's the very reason they all want Siasha dead. After yet another violent battle for her life, she teams up with Zig, a mercenary, and they depart for unknown lands to find somewhere she can live in peace. But is the pair any match for the lost magic and vicious monstrosities that lie ahead?

Shinpei Ezaki ( Vivy -Fluorite Eye's Song- , Hanebad! , Monster Strike The Movie ) is directing the anime at 8-Bit . Taishirou Tanimura ( Ace of Diamond , Sakura Trick episode scripts) is in charge of series scripts, Keita Matsumoto ( Bungaku Shōjo film, Persona 5 the Animation -The Day Breakers- , Shining Hearts ) is designing the characters, Akiko Fujita ( Dorohedoro , The Elusive Samurai , Jujutsu Kaisen ) is the sound director, and Rei Ishizuka ( A Couple of Cuckoos , With You and the Rain , PriPara ) is composing the music at Lantis .

Chōhōkiteki began serializing the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in June 2021, and ended it in December 2022. Micro Magazine published the first print volume with illustrations by Bench Kanase in May 2023. Micro Magazine published the seventh volume on January 20, and will publish the eighth volume on September 24.

Makoto Miyagi launched a manga adaptation of the story on Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket manga app in January 2024. Kodansha 's K MANGA service is publishing the manga in English.

title: Witch and the Mercenary Anime Reveals First Trailer, New Cast, April 2027 Release
content:
Witch and the Mercenary anime revealed the first main trailer, along with two new teaser visuals, three additional cast members, and an April 2027 release date.

The newly announced cast members are:

• Yuri Noguchi as Isana Geihorn

• Hiromu Mineta as Alan Close

• Haruka Shiraishi as Elsia Amet

Taito Ban stars as Zig Crane, with Saori Hayami voicing Siasha. You can hear the cast in the new trailer.

Two new teaser visuals were also released, one focusing on Siasha and the other on Zig. Both images pay homage to the cover artwork of the first volume of the original light novel.

The story follows the two after beginning as enemies, with the solitary witch and lone mercenary eventually traveling together in search of a place where they can live. Shinpei Ezaki is directing the anime at studio 8bit. Daishiro Tanimura is handling series composition, Keita Matsumoto is the character designer, and Rei Ishizuka is composing the music.

The anime is based on the light novel series byChohokiteki Kaeru, with original character designs by Kanose Bench. There is also a manga adaptation by Makoto Miyagi. Seven Seas Entertainment licensed both, describing the story: Nothing in this world is more dangerous than a witch. The epitome of fear and terror, they can summon floods on a whim, conjure balls of fire out of the air, or even destroy entire countries overnight. Incur their wrath, and no one is safe. At least, that’s what everyone thinks, and it’s the very reason they all want Siasha dead. After yet another violent battle for her life, she teams up with Zig, a mercenary, and they depart for unknown lands to find somewhere she can live in peace. But is the pair any match for the lost magic and vicious monstrosities that lie ahead?

title: 'Majo to Youhei' Reveals Additional Cast, Staff, First Promo for Spring 2027
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Kaeru Chouhoukiteki 's Majo to Youhei ( Witch and Mercenary ) light novel revealed additional cast, start, a second teaser visual (pictured), and the first promotional video on Wednesday. The anime series will premiere on 30 NTV stations and BS NTV in April 2027.

Cast Isana Geihorn: Yuri Noguchi ( Ryza no Atelier ) Alan Clowes: Hiromu Mineta ( Katainaka no Ossan, Kensei ni Naru ) Eksis Ahmet: Haruka Shiraishi ( Clevatess )

Staff Assistant Series Composition: Shingo Irie ( Chi. Chikyuu no Undou ni Tsuite series composition) Sub-Character Design: Hideki Sakai ( Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken 2nd Season chief animation director) Monster Design: Wataru Inata ( Sentai Red Isekai de Boukensha ni Naru ), Ryou Hirata ( Zenshuu. sub-character design) Chief Animation Directors: Keita Matsumoto ( Persona 5 the Animation: The Day Breakers ), Hideki Sakai, Sorato Shimizu ( Blue Lock ) Art: Marunaga Shoten Art Director: Kazuhiro Inoue ( Ookami to Koushinryou: Merchant Meets the Wise Wolf ) Prop Design: Mikio ( Kusuriya no Hitorigoto ) Image Board: pomodorosa ( Deca-Dence original character design) Color Design: Kunio Tsujita ( Tokyo Revengers ) Director of Photography: Shuuhei Inabe ( Do It Yourself!! photography) CG Director: Fuuma Aizawa ( Shy ) Editing: Gou Sadamatsu ( Shangri-La Frontier )

Shinpei Ezaki ( Vivy: Fluorite Eye's Song ) directs the anime at 8Bit . Daishirou Tanimura ( Hell Mode ) is handling the series composition and Keita Matsumoto ( Persona 5 the Animation: The Day Breakers ) is designing the characters. Rei Ishizuka ( Ayakashi Triangle ) is composing the music.

Chouhoukiteki began penning the action fantasy novel on Shousetsuka ni Narou in June 2021. Micro Magazine began publishing the light novel under its GCN Bunko imprint with illustrations by Bench Kanase in May 2023. The seventh volume went on sale on January 20, with the eighth volume scheduled for a September 24 release. Majo to Youhei has a cumulative 1.7 million copies in circulation.

Makoto Miyagi began drawing a manga adaptation on the Magazine Pocket service in January 2024. Kodansha released the ninth volume on August 7.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the light novel in English in February 2024 and published the first part of the sixth volume on April 28. The seventh volume is planned to be released on November 24. Kodansha publishes the manga digitally in English on its K Manga app and website.

title: 5 Years Ago, Berserk Released Its Final Chapter From Its Legendary Creator, But Their Legacy Lives On
content:
There’s no denying the impact that Kentaro Miura’s work has had on manga readers around the globe. Of his work, his most prolific, Berserk , is often cited as being one of the most influential and prolific seinen series in the world, acting as a touchstone for other massive pieces of media, including multiple FromSoftware titles like Dark Souls , Bloodborne , and Elden Ring . Even other mangaka, like Attack on Titan ‘s Hajime Isayama and Blue Exorcist ‘s Kazue Kato have cited Berserk as being a point of reference for the respective works.

In 2021, the final chapter of Berserk penned by Miura, Chapter 364, “Teardrop of Morning Dew,” released in Young Animal Issue #18. Aside from the chapter being notable for being Miura’s final entry into the series, the chapter has stuck with fans for its defining quote delivered by a mysterious child who visits Guts and Casca, stating: “…When I wake from the dream, only a vague sense of longing remains… that too, will soon disappear… with a single tear like morning dew.” The quote itself has lingered with fans for years, even as Berserk continues under the direction of Kouji Mori .

Miura’s Legacy Was Cemented In Guts’ Journey & A Deep Love For Art

Kentaro Miura launched Berserk ‘s prototype, aptly titled Berserk: The Prototype in 1988. The brief one-shot was published in Hakusensha’s Monthly ComiComi , while he was still working as an assistant to Hajime no Ippo ‘s creator George Morikawa. Miura has originally envisioned Berserk to be a fantasy series designed for shonen audiences, and didn’t have many plans in place for where he wanted the story to go. In spite of this, he continued shaping the world and journey that Guts would inevitably go on as the years went on. One thing Kentaro Miura has always been very firm and very open about was his influences when creating Berserk .

Deeply inspired by other pieces of dark literature, Miura’s set pieces for Berserk were influenced by works like Clive Barker’s Hellraiser , Jean-Jacques Annaud’s The Name of the Rose , and Brothers Grimm’s fairytales, while the art style he honed for the series was deeply inspired by Fist of the North Star by Buronson and Tetsuo Hara. Miura’s myriad of inspirations show that the mangaka is true lover of all corners of art and media, embracing themes and visuals that, while off-putting to mainstream audiences can really resonate with the right crowd. His story writing speaks to this as well, as Guts’ journey is overflowing with themes regarding the indomitable will of humanity in the face of suffering, free will, and hope born from the desperation of survival.

Berserk ‘s Impact Has Kept Miura’s Memory Alive

As of writing, it’s been reported that there are over 70 million copies of Berserk in circulation around the globe. Officially being serialized since 1989, the series very quickly became popular both in sales and among critics, with even western publications like Rolling Stone giving the manga glowing reviews, calling Berserk a poignant exploration of humanity, friendship and ambition . Artistically, Miura has been praised for decades for his intricate detailing techniques, using meticulous cross-hatching methods to give an almost obsessive attention to detail in every single panel of the manga.

This masterful presentation has made an impact on creatives around the world, with many dark fantasy mangaka, like Black Butler ‘s Yana Toboso, Attack on Titan ‘s Hajime Isayama, Blue Exorcist ‘s Kazue Kato, and Vinland Saga ‘s Makoto Yukimura declaring that they’ve taken inspiration from the work. Even in western media, Adi Shankar, who worked on the first four seasons of Netflix’s Castlevania has called Berserk a masterpiece , stating that it would be a dream to work on an adaptation of the series. With Berserk in the hands of Miura’s personal friend and colleague Kouji Mori and the rest of Studio Gaga, it’s clear the series won’t be going anywhere anytime soon, and that the people who love and respected Miura are hard at work to keep his memory alive.

As of writing, it’s been reported that there are over 70 million copies of Berserk in circulation around the globe. Officially being serialized since 1989, the series very quickly became popular both in sales and among critics, with even western publications like Rolling Stone giving the manga glowing reviews, calling Berserk a poignant exploration of humanity, friendship and ambition . Artistically, Miura has been praised for decades for his intricate detailing techniques, using meticulous cross-hatching methods to give an almost obsessive attention to detail in every single panel of the manga.

This masterful presentation has made an impact on creatives around the world, with many dark fantasy mangaka, like Black Butler ‘s Yana Toboso, Attack on Titan ‘s Hajime Isayama, Blue Exorcist ‘s Kazue Kato, and Vinland Saga ‘s Makoto Yukimura declaring that they’ve taken inspiration from the work. Even in western media, Adi Shankar, who worked on the first four seasons of Netflix’s Castlevania has called Berserk a masterpiece , stating that it would be a dream to work on an adaptation of the series. With Berserk in the hands of Miura’s personal friend and colleague Kouji Mori and the rest of Studio Gaga, it’s clear the series won’t be going anywhere anytime soon, and that the people who love and respected Miura are hard at work to keep his memory alive.

title: Val x Love's Ryōsuke Asakura Launches New Manga Series
content:
Ryōsuke Asakura launched a new manga series titled Evangeline Puts on Shoes ( Evangeline wa Kutsu o Haku) on Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ platform on Wednesday.

The story follows popular high school student and actress Evangeline. While everyone is dazzled by her looks and charm, only the plain Kotarō; an aspiring shoemaker, can see the pain in her footsteps.

Asakura launched the Anastacia no Ikita 9-kakan ( The Last 9 Days of Anastasia ) manga in Square Enix 's Monthly Shonen Gangan magazine in February 2024 and ended it on September 12, 2025. Square Enix shipped the third and final volume on November 12, 2025.

Asakura launched the Shikizaki Shimai wa Abakaretai ( I Want to Be Exposed by the Shikizaki Sisters ) manga in Shueisha 's Weekly Young Jump magazine in December 2021 and ended it in April 2023. Shueisha published the manga's fifth and final volume in June 2023.

Asakura's launched the Val x Love ( Ikusa x Koi ) manga in Monthly Shonen Gangan in December 2015 and ended it in March 2023. Square Enix published the manga's 16th and final volume in May 2023, and Yen Press published that final volume in English in March 2024. The manga inspired a television anime that premiered in October 2019. Sentai Filmworks streamed the anime on HIDIVE as it aired in Japan, and released the anime on Blu-ray Disc in November 2020.
